title: Root to Leaf Sum
statement:
A **leaf** is a node with no children. Is there a path that starts at the root, goes down through children, ends at a **leaf**, and has node values that add up to exactly `target`?

Return `true` or `false`. An empty tree has no such path.

examples.explanation: The path 10 -> 5 -> 7 ends at the leaf 7 and adds up to 22.
10 -> 5 adds up to 15, but 5 is not a leaf (it has children 3 and 7), so that path does not count.

hints.nudge: Each time you go down to a child, the sum you still need changes. By how much?
hints.pattern: Recursion: subtract the node's value from the target and ask the same question about each child; stop at a leaf.
hints.pseudocode:
has_leaf_sum(node, target):
  if node is missing: return false
  if node has no children: return node.val == target
  return has_leaf_sum(node.left, target - node.val) or has_leaf_sum(node.right, target - node.val)
hints.walkthrough: Walk down from the root and keep track of how much of the target is still needed: when you step onto a node, subtract its value. A missing child contributes no path at all, so it answers false. At a leaf, the path is complete, so what is left must equal the leaf's own value (or equivalently the remaining target must be exactly 0 after subtracting it). At any other node, a path exists if one exists through the left child or through the right child. Be careful not to accept a node that has only one child as if it were a leaf. Every node is visited at most once: O(n) time, O(height) recursion depth.
